executive_assessment.text: Hazard maps place greatest river-flood risk along Nepal’s southern border and valleys, plus heat, drought, landslide, and air pollution.
With 62% of workers in agriculture, Terai rainfed smallholders face floods; limited safety nets constrain coping.

The NDC sets adaptation priorities across agriculture and food security, forests and watersheds, water and energy, settlements, infrastructure, tourism and heritage, health, and disaster risk reduction.

geographic_notes.text: Nepal; Terai; floodplains: With 62% of workers in agriculture, Terai rainfed smallholders face floods; limited safety nets constrain coping.
southern border; river valleys: Hazard maps place greatest river-flood risk along Nepal’s southern border and valleys, plus heat, drought, landslide, and air pollution.
southern municipalities; Nepal: Over 4.3 million people fall in the extreme heat-stress category for a modeled 20-year event, concentrated in southern municipalities.
Lumbini; Karnali; Sudurpaschim; western Nepal: Mid-century CMIP6 projections show larger extreme-precipitation changes in western Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim than farther east.

known_gaps.text: No inspected Nepal source explicitly links climate hazards to conflict or violence; no climate-FCV pathway is asserted.
